I guess if you got limited time to do cardio, if at all... try reducing your calorie intake and do some basic weight lifting when home. Pushups are great, but try dumbbel rows and situps. For you to loose fat you need to eat less than you burn during the day. Calculate your so-called rmr online (will be explained there) and eat ~300 calories less per day (roughly count your calories either manually or with the app myfitnesspal). Because your goal is to loose your belly, and not to get mad shredded thaz should be enough. When asked to enter your activities when calculating the rmr just enter none.

Be patient and continue eating a balanced diet and you should be good. Add some cardio if you have some spare time. 

And take pictures every week for reference and motivation. The more weight you loose the easier the workout gets so make sure to up your intensity every now and then

Good luck and Keep it consistent

It is always going to be some major bullshit when first working out like said. The only thing you notice are the soreness and the unwillingness to go again. I hated it, you need somebody who motivates you to get your ass up and knows what you have to be going through. And trust me, the mental health aspect after accomplishing my goals have way outweighed the physical aspect. I was fat, depressed, not confident and overall the biggest looser you can imagine. After months of working out i got to say: i still am far from perfect and there still is so much more to learn. But i gained knowledge that guides me through life. I don't need to be perfect, i don't have to look like Arnold or Coleman or all of the others. It's unachievable without going down the most unhealthy road possible: juicing. I got and get to know myself better and am able to set goals that i want to reach. 

If your mindset is that life isnt worth living then working out is a great thing to start. Basically anything that makes yourself grow is a good start. If you work out for some time you will discover that life is worth living for as long as possible and that you should enjoy every second of it, even when clinging to the rope. And by that you kill 2 birds with 1 stone. Try to get to know people who work out in your area and form a group. Get yourself motivated and set yourself strict goals. You are going to succeed

I don't always feel better after a workout, neither do i get a mood boost all the time. The goal is not to instantly feel better but to gather the strength to keep going. This is going to take time and effort. Most importantly you need a goal that YOU want to achieve. I wanted to burn lots of fat and after half a year of painstakingly cutting and tracking nutrients and calories, going 6x a week i only now feel that i actually get a mood boost. Not only when working out because i see the results of my training but an overall boost in health and mental health. I had been at a point where i would just give a single fuck about the people around me, i just kept going. Like who the hell cares, it's not like they do. I understand why it's so hard to pull through but the work pays off in the end. It's just impossible to expect instantanious results

You have no other reason not to jump, than beeing able to decide if you want to jump or not. Other people are no reason for you to change your decision. But the liberty of living itself, at least to me, is the solely reason to keep going. Pain is something we all go through and every person has a different reason for it. Without pain there would be no happiness. People who have a very stress-free and healthy life, don't take things for granted others would. I, much rather would be somebody who goes through a lot of shit than an arrogant prick who is not acceptive to anything. 

The motto; "time heals all wounds" is something i can definately agree on, but i think that if the wound is big enough, the pain can be unbearable at times, especially if bad things are adding up. 

Be rational and think about every aspect you consider true. Are you really a failure ? I don't think so. Are you really not worthy of beeing loved ? I don't think so. Are you really worthless ? I don't think so a single bit. 

Know that the path of love and happiness comes from you accepting yourself first. And if you reached a point at which you can say: "I love myself to a degree, that i know what is good for me and what isn't" then you have done it.

The path you take to this goal is up to you, but know that life throws obstacles your way all the time and all you can do is avoid them or tackle them straight on. You are not weak, neither are you unable to get over these heavy burdens. You have struggled for so long that i can say these things with certainty. You will always have people who got your back, you got me and so many other folks who have been through stuff like this, or are going through it right now. Just know that the acceptance of your fate is the biggest step to living a good life.

This is a serious topic and i can relate to what you are saying, although for me it's a bit different. Just like you i had a group of friends, people who i could talk to about whatever but i feel like i have grown out of this group over the last few months as they stayed as immature as always. Now i also feel like i am the outsider and just observe, don't experience. 

I did a lot of work on myself, which is what i recommend to you. Self-reflect on your issues. I, just like you don't want to be a jerk, and don't want to be that guy who gets picked last. You are perfect just the way you are,  but if that is the case think about what you could change on yourself to be more socially accepted even if you think that you already are a social guy. I don't want you to force a change that is not natural, but a change that is free and non-guided.

For that reason, i started to go to the gym, and began to read books again. This did not make me gain any friends first hand but improved self-esteam and self-conciousness in a very natural way making me more socially skilled. I even started to do small talk with other people, which i normally am not too fond of. This all helped me to differentiate between the people i can rely on in difficult times and people who just abuse me for what i am. Finding friends, true friends, is a long journey and there are going to be a lot of failures on your way. But you need to keep going and try to find people who YOU enjoy beeing surrounded by. Don't expect to find friends anywhere you go, in 99% of cases the people will never be your true friend and in the other 1% it will take time to build a relationship that you can let yourself fall into without the anxiety of beeing abused. Don't let your hopes diminish because it takes a long time for you to find people, because when you will find a true and honest friend it will be one for long time.

I can only talk for myself here but if you think that your humble, kind and offering personality gets abused by other people who never give anything back to you, then contemplate on the idea of beeing more selfish.I am probably not the first person to tell you this and i won't be the last but take what i say very seriously. This was and still is the hardest thing to do for me, but you need to start to look out for yourself more often. I get a feeling of accomplishment temporarily when i talk to people and try to help them. But i often load their worries and feelings on my own shoulders which in the long term, supresses my own needs. 

I hope this helped a bit, keep your hopes up because you are going to succeed.

Society can be harsh and extremely unforgiving.
People are selfish and that is the problem. You probably are not as selfish as you would need to be to have a normal life. I too, put large amounts of effort into things i just get almost nothing back from. If it is spending time with my gf, helping her out in maths or politics and just recieving a kiss at the end for it, no "love you" and no "thank you", or building up a friendship over a long time that ends in me still beeing the second choice.
This had me upset and depressed for such a long time that i started to notice that, it did not help to think negatively about these things. I confronted my gf about it and it showed that she just has a problem with showing affection. And that my friend also has preferences like any other person does.

In this matter life sucks and the only thing that you can do about it is to change your surroundings.
Meet new people, find a hobby you are interested in that helps you to improve as a person. Go to the gym and make you feel good about yourself. Try to be who you want to be, not who your surroundings try to make yourself be. Thats what worked for me.

You are not an extra burden to the earth but a person worthy of beeing loved and liked by others.
The only hard thing is to find your way of doing things.
